Dickenson County, Virginia Tax Sales: Simple Guide for First-Time Property Investors

Thinking about buying real estate through a tax sale in Dickenson County, Virginia? These auctions are a great way to purchase property while helping the county recover unpaid taxes. If you’re just getting started, here’s a clear breakdown of how the process works.

Click Here to Get Dustin Hahn’s Tax Lien and Deed FREE Mini-Course

When Dickenson County Holds Tax Sales

Dickenson County doesn’t follow a yearly schedule. Sales are organized as needed when tax-delinquent properties become available.

  • Timing: No fixed date
  • Stay Updated: Watch for public notices and check our Auction calendar

Auction Time and Location

Each auction listing includes the exact date and time.

  • Typical Start Time: 10:00 AM (Eastern Time)
  • Where It Happens:
    • Meeting Room outside the Treasurer’s Office
    • Address: 818 Happy Valley Drive, Clintwood, VA 24228

Registration Requirements

You must register in advance if you want to bid.

  • When to Register:
    • Registration opens once the auction is announced
    • Deadlines are included in the official notice
  • Why It Matters: Unregistered bidders can’t participate

Property Redemption Deadline

Property owners still have time to redeem their property before the auction.

  • Redemption Ends: On the day of the auction
  • How to Redeem: They must pay all taxes, interest, penalties, and legal costs in full

Bidding Process and Payment Terms

Winning a bid means you’ll need to pay a deposit and follow the sale terms exactly.

  • Who Wins: Highest bidder
  • Starting Bid: Usually begins at the assessed or appraised value
  • Deposit:
    • 25% of the winning bid or $1,000 (whichever is greater)
  • Buyer’s Premium:
    • 10% added to the final bid
  • Accepted Payments: Check the sale notice for approved payment types

Where to Find Auction Updates

Stay informed about upcoming sales:

  • Visit: Dickenson County Real Estate Tax Sale Page

Smart Tips for First-Time Bidders

Use these tips to stay ahead:

  • Research historical backgrounds; properties here often carry a rich local story.
  • Verify the state of local services, including road conditions, before finalizing your bid.
  • Consult a local inspector to uncover any issues that aren’t immediately obvious.
  • Factor in future development by checking with county planning staff.
